204 No Content on Delete

A successful delete has nothing left to send back — the status code says so on its own.

Every other successful response so far sends a body — the created/updated/ fetched resource, wrapped in sendResource (first topic). A delete is different: once a row is gone, there's no resource left to describe. REST's answer is 204 No Content — a success status that comes with an explicitly empty body, rather than 200 with, say, { "data": null } standing in for nothing.

// Figure 3.10: no body, just a status (src/controllers/ticket.controller.js, excerpt)
export const deleteTicket = asyncHandler(async (req, res) => {
  const existing = await ticketService.getTicketById(req.params.id);

  if (!existing) {
    throw new ApiError(404, `Ticket ${req.params.id} not found`);
  }

  await ticketService.deleteTicket(req.params.id);
  res.status(204).end();
});

res.status(204).end(), not res.status(204).json(...) — calling .json() here would still send a body (even .json(null) sends the four bytes null), which technically contradicts what 204 promises. .end() closes the response with no body at all, which is the only combination that matches the status code's own meaning. Every DELETE route in this project — tickets, comments, tags — ends its controller the same way.
